lesson.title: Learning PINNs in PyTorch: Diffusion Equation
lesson.goal: train a physics-informed neural network in PyTorch

sources.title: Learning PINNs in PyTorch: Diffusion Equation

steps.title: Install pyDOE and import libraries
steps.instructions: Install pyDOE and import PyTorch, Matplotlib, NumPy, and lhs. Configure device and fixed random seeds in pinn_diffusion.py.

targets.caption: Import PyTorch and Latin Hypercube Sampling

explanations.topic: Purpose of pyDOE and Latin Hypercube Sampling

hints: Which sampling library is needed for collocation points?
Run !pip install pyDOE and import lhs from pyDOE.
Add torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float), manual_seed(1234), and device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu').
common_mistakes: Forgetting to install pyDOE before importing lhs.
Using float64 instead of setting default dtype to torch.float (float32).

steps.title: Generate and plot exact solution
steps.instructions: Define f_real(x,t) for the analytical solution and create a 2D meshgrid over x in [-1,1] and t in [0,1].

targets.caption: Define f_real and generate space-time grid

hints: How do you build a 2D space-time grid from 1D tensors in PyTorch?
Use torch.linspace(-1,1,200) for x, torch.linspace(0,1,100) for t, and torch.meshgrid(x,t).
Define def f_real(x,t): return torch.exp(-t)*(torch.sin(np.pi*x)) and call plot3D(x,t,y_real).
common_mistakes: Using wrong domain bounds instead of [-1, 1] for x and [0, 1] for t.
Calling numpy functions instead of torch.exp and torch.sin on PyTorch tensors.

steps.title: Flatten grid into testing tensors
steps.instructions: Flatten X, T, and y_real into column vectors x_test and y_test using torch.hstack, and extract domain bounds lb and ub.

targets.caption: Flatten 2D grid into column vectors for evaluation

explanations.topic: Column-major flattening for fully connected networks

hints: Why does a fully connected network need flattened vectors instead of 2D matrices?
Transpose X, T, and y_real with .transpose(1,0), flatten, and add a trailing axis with [:,None].
Stack X and T with torch.hstack and set lb=X_test[0], ub=X_test[-1].
common_mistakes: Omitting [:,None], which leaves y_test as 1D instead of shape (20000, 1).
Forgetting .transpose(1,0) before .flatten() when reshaping back later.

steps.title: Build initial and boundary data
steps.instructions: Create initial and boundary condition tensors, stack them with torch.vstack, and sample Nu=100 training points.

targets.caption: Combine initial and boundary conditions and sample Nu training points

explanations.topic: Boundary conditions at x=-1 and x=1

hints: Which slices of X and T correspond to t=0, x=1, and x=-1?
Use X[:,0] for t=0, X[-1,:] for bottom, and X[0,:] for top, then vstack them.
Sample Nu=100 indices via np.random.choice(X_train.shape[0], Nu, replace=False).
common_mistakes: Using torch.hstack instead of torch.vstack when combining left, bottom, and top points.
Forgetting .unsqueeze(1) on left_Y so its shape matches bottom_Y and top_Y.
Setting replace=True when sampling unique boundary points.

steps.title: Sample collocation points with LHS
steps.instructions: Sample Nf=10000 interior collocation points using lhs(2, Nf), stack them with initial/boundary points, and move data to device.

targets.caption: Sample interior domain collocation points using Latin Hypercube Sampling

explanations.topic: Latin Hypercube Sampling for collocation points
Why f_hat is a tensor of zeros

hints: How do you map lhs(2, Nf) from [0,1] into [lb, ub]?
Compute lb + (ub - lb) * lhs(2, Nf) and vstack with X_train_Nu.
Convert X_train_Nu, X_train_Nf, Y_train_Nu with .float().to(device) and set f_hat=torch.zeros(X_train_Nf.shape[0],1).to(device).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to append X_train_Nu to X_train_Nf.
Leaving lhs output as double (float64) without calling .float() before passing to the network.
Creating f_hat on CPU instead of moving it to device.

steps.title: Define the FCN neural network
steps.instructions: Implement the FCN neural network with Tanh activations, lossBC, and lossPDE using autograd.grad with create_graph=True.

targets.caption: Compute derivatives using autograd.grad and calculate PINN physics loss

explanations.topic: FCN architecture, Xavier init, and forward pass
Boundary loss and PDE residual via autograd

hints: How do you compute first and second derivatives of the network output with respect to (x, t)?
Clone x_PDE, set g.requires_grad=True, and call autograd.grad twice with create_graph=True.
Extract f_t = f_x_t[:,[1]] and f_xx = f_xx_tt[:,[0]], compute the residual f, and return self.loss_function(f, f_hat).
common_mistakes: Forgetting create_graph=True on autograd.grad, which breaks backpropagation through second derivatives.
Forgetting g.requires_grad=True on the cloned collocation tensor.
Swapping column indices 0 (x) and 1 (t) when slicing f_x_t and f_xx_tt.

steps.title: Instantiate PINN and Adam optimizer
steps.instructions: Instantiate PINN on device with layer architecture [2, 32, 32, 1] and initialize the Adam optimizer.

targets.caption: Instantiate the PINN model and set up the Adam optimizer

explanations.topic: Input/output dimensions of the PINN architecture

hints: What must the first and last numbers in layers be?
Use np.array([2,32,64,1]) since the inputs are (x, t) and the output is y.
Instantiate optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(PINN.parameters(), lr=1e-3, amsgrad=False).
common_mistakes: Using a positive exponent in lr=1e3 instead of lr=1e-3.
Forgetting to call PINN.to(device) before creating the optimizer or running training.

steps.title: Train the network and log loss
steps.instructions: Run the training loop updating PINN parameters via loss.backward() and optimizer.step(), logging metrics to terminal.

targets.caption: Execute optimization loop with zero_grad, backward, and step

explanations.topic: Using torch.no_grad() when logging test loss

hints: Did you move X_test and y_test to device before logging test_loss?
Call loss = PINN.loss(X_train_Nu, Y_train_Nu, X_train_Nf), zero_grad(), backward(), and step().
Wrap test_loss = PINN.lossBC(X_test, y_test) inside with torch.no_grad(): and print both losses.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to move X_test and y_test to device before evaluating test_loss.
Omitting optimizer.zero_grad(), causing gradients to accumulate across iterations.
Forgetting with torch.no_grad(): during test evaluation.

steps.title: Evaluate and plot predicted solution
steps.instructions: Evaluate PINN predictions across x_test and plot or save the solution comparison against the analytical reference.

targets.caption: Evaluate trained model and save comparison plot

explanations.topic: Reshaping vector predictions back into 2D matrices

hints: How do you turn the 20000-element prediction vector back into a 2D plot grid?
Reshape each tensor to [100, 200], transpose(1,0), and call .detach().cpu().
Call plot3D_Matrix(arr_x1, arr_t1, arr_y1) and compare with plot3D_Matrix(X, T, y_real).
common_mistakes: Reshaping to [200, 100] instead of [100, 200] before transposing.
Forgetting .detach().cpu() before plotting GPU tensors with Matplotlib.
